title: Uniform Inference for Lagged Recurrent-Event Effects under Rare Exposure Switching

gap_reasons: The delivered contribution is exact switch-score centering, uniform nuisance learning, and regime-specific inference within a preassigned, known-protocol, independently stopped Poisson model; it does not establish a general weak-positivity SNCURE theorem. The discordance rate and Poisson count reduction specialize classical rare-selection machinery, including [Le Cam's approximation theorem](https://msp.org/pjm/1960/10-4/pjm-v10-n4-p11-p.pdf), rather than introduce a broadly new framework. The TL;DR and project justification advertise matched full-class bounds without carrying Theorem 3's qualification to fixed specifications admitting Proposition 1's feasible contrast segment; nonempty coefficient-domain interiors alone do not establish that converse. The efficiency and joint-experiment statements are confined to fixed strict-interior baselines, while conditional likelihood coverage is asymptotic and supplies no finite-regime optimality guarantee. The projected score is constrained by this specialized scope and by an exponential-size theoretical learner without a delivered computational implementation or evidence supporting the proposed bootstrap replacement. proof_attempt_summary: The discovery run derived rare-switch risks, honest intervals, exact stopped-Poisson factorization, feasible inference, and finite-direction Gaussian/marked-Poisson limits on a preassigned known-protocol independent-clock benchmark. The joint-experiment gap was discharged and all seven classical cited leaves were source-attested, including a repaired generic-LAN scalar convolution reduction; final math review passed, but novelty remained incremental below the field floor (6.1 < 7.4). An unconsumed duplicate theorem and summary prose omitting the feasible-segment lower-bound qualification remain disclosed; no F-stage or Lean certification was attempted, and no unchanged-scope retry is recommended.
tldr: Persistent exposure histories can leave separate causal lag effects weakly measured even in a large recurrent-event cohort. In the specified independently stopped Poisson benchmark, the cumulative blip \(s\) remains regular, whereas the contrast \(b\) is governed by \(n\delta_n\). The note combines survival-weighted efficient information and an observable attaining score with a complete-mark critical likelihood experiment, matched full-class risk and honest-length orders, and conditional simulation-test inversion. Exact centering and a distribution-free clipped learner permit arbitrary baseline supports and nonsmooth known switch weights. Joint finite-direction likelihood convergence and nuisance-space closure are established at fixed jointly feasible strict-interior baselines; global process convergence for arbitrary moving nuisances remains outside scope.
gap: Fixed-law causal recurrent-rate asymptotics do not justify collapsing-history information or confidence calibration at finite discordance. Generic Poissonization supplies part of the reduction but no feasible full-class causal benchmark.
fill: The same observed-law class supports the regular cumulative coefficient, the weak contrast, a uniform learner, an attaining leading-information score, and honest confidence procedures in all switch regimes.
